title.narrative: Safeguarding the Ancient City of Aleppo: Emergency Stabilization, Capacity Building, and Livelihood Support for Sustainable Cultural Heritage Management

description.narrative: The present project pursues two complementary objectives that connect conservation and protection of cultural heritage to economic recovery. First, the project aims to refine and structuralize existing damage assessment data pertaining cultural properties located within the Ancient City of Aleppo. Such data has been developed by UNESCO and other organizations since the outset of the conflict. In this context, the project will take stock of this documentation and consolidate the existing data. Emergency stabilization and basic repairs will follow immediately, delivered through cash-for-work scheme that pairs skilled professionals with young apprentices. In this way, stabilization works will support employment and hands-on training, giving Alepines both the means and the expertise to carry forward longer-term restoration once the project closes. Second, the project will restore the ability of Aleppo’s cultural institutions to protect, record and share their collections. Museums and heritage directorates will receive modern digitization equipment and targeted instruction in cataloguing and preventive conservation. With these tools, staff will be able to create a comprehensive digital register of artefacts, monitor their condition, and cooperate effectively with customs and security agencies to combat illicit trafficking. Strengthened in this way, local institutions will possess the resilience and knowledge base required to lead Syria’s wider cultural recovery and to turn heritage stewardship into a sustainable livelihood sector. Taken together, these twin objectives—physical stabilization that generates jobs, and institutional digitization that safeguards collections—ensure that Aleppo’s heritage revival is both a cultural imperative and a catalyst for economic renewal.
